clue.text: Storyteller's model answer rejected

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the joined words are read from right to left

parts.note: to model is to pose for an artist
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: A storyteller's ideal reply is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: POSE plus A read backwards gives AESOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aesop is the ancient Greek teller of fables, the archetypal storyteller.

clue.text: Suitable duties wasted talents

indicators.note: wasted suggests ruined or broken down, so the letters before it are rearranged

parts.note: apt means suitable
the word duties with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's gifts were squandered on tasks that merely fitted the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Aptitudes are natural abilities or gifts, which is what talents are.

clue.text: Bit of toothpaste inside mug

indicators.note: a bit of the phrase means only a stretch of its running letters is taken

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A dollop of toothpaste has ended up in a drinking mug.
explanation.definitionFit: A stein is a large earthenware beer mug of German origin.

clue.text: Recipe's roughly accurate

indicators.note: roughly means not in exact form, so the preceding letters are loosely rearranged

parts.note: the word with its S, all seven letters used

explanation.surface: A cook judges that the recipe is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: The irony is that 'roughly' and the answer are opposites.
explanation.definitionFit: Precise and accurate are synonyms, both meaning exact and correct in detail.

clue.text: Understanding group of people

definitions.meaning: second meaning: an assembly or meeting

explanation.surface: A sympathetic crowd of people.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs the words as an adjective and noun; they are really two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both concluding or inferring something and an assembled crowd or meeting of persons.

clue.text: Crushed golf ball's shape?

parts.note: Golf is the NATO alphabet word for G
a ball is round in shape

explanation.surface: A golf ball that has been squashed out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground is the past participle of grind, so it describes something crushed to powder.

clue.text: Right-wingers embracing the man's ideas

indicators.note: embracing means hugging, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: Tories are members of Britain's right-wing Conservative Party
he is the pronoun for a man

explanation.surface: Conservatives taking on board a particular man's thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Theories are proposed explanations or systems of thought, so they are ideas.

clue.text: Old writers finally take charge

parts.note: ex means former or old
pens are writing instruments

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the next word, so only its closing letter counts

parts.note: the last letter of take

explanation.surface: Retired authors at last assume control.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take charge' looks like a phrase, but charge stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An expense is a cost or fee, and a charge is money demanded for something.

clue.text: Overwhelmed? I'm crushed

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
pressed means squashed

explanation.surface: Someone asked if they were overwhelmed replies that they are devastated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be impressed is to be strongly struck or awed, close to overwhelmed with admiration.

clue.text: Females and American soldiers holding hands

indicators.note: holding means gripping something within, so one part sits inside the other

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers
the two hands are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: Women and US servicemen walking hand in hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls are young women, so the word names females.

clue.text: So concerning after the golfer's shout

indicators.note: after sets the word for concerning behind the word the, overturning the clue's order

parts.note: taken as written
re means about or concerning
golfers shout fore to warn of a ball in flight

explanation.surface: A query about what follows a golfer's warning cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golfer's shout' is the warning cry players yell when a ball heads towards people.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and so are both conjunctions meaning consequently or for that reason.

clue.text: In Puerto Rico, copy set of examination questions

indicators.note: in places the next word inside the letters that follow

parts.note: PR is the abbreviation for Puerto Rico
to ape is to imitate or copy

explanation.surface: A student in Puerto Rico cribbing an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts 'copy' inside the place; the wordplay does exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam paper is the printed list of questions candidates must answer.

clue.text: X is turned on, creating anxiety

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

indicators.note: turned means flipped round, so the little word before it runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being flipped
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone getting excited and making others nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turned on' reads as a phrase, but only 'is' is turned; ON is taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental strain or nervousness, which is a form of anxiety.

clue.text: King annoys football team

parts.note: R stands for Rex, Latin for king
angers means annoys

explanation.surface: The monarch is irritating a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Rangers is a Glasgow football club; Queens Park Rangers is a London one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rangers is the name of a well-known Scottish soccer club, so it is an example of a team.

clue.text: The woman breaks Detective Inspector's plates

indicators.note: breaks means splits open, so one word is wedged into the middle of the other

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector, plus the S of the possessive
she is the pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: A woman smashes a police inspector's crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaks' suggests smashing crockery, but it signals one piece splitting another.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishes are flat vessels for serving food, as plates are.

clue.text: Give up resistance in the grip of nurse with red pants

indicators.note: being in the grip of something means being held inside it
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the words before it are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written, as fodder
taken as written, as fodder
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A nurse in red trousers gives in to opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers (British pants are underwear) but is slang for rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to yield or hand over, which is to give up.

clue.text: Embarrassed about rental agreement getting published

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red
a lease is a contract for renting property

explanation.surface: A blushing tenant whose lease has gone public.
explanation.definitionFit: Released means made available to the public, as a book or record is when issued.

clue.text: Possibly dim editor is tickled pink

parts.note: read whimsically as de-light, to take the light away, which is one way to dim
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A rather dense editor is thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' flags a playful reading: to de-light something is to remove its light, i.e. dim it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tickled pink is an idiom for being highly pleased, which is what delighted means.

clue.text: Tries steaming pet's mat? About time!

indicators.note: about means around, so the jumbled letters go around the final piece
steaming is slang for very drunk, so the words that follow are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of both words, apostrophe dropped
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone is finally getting round to steam-cleaning the pet's mat.
explanation.definitionFit: Attempts are efforts to do something, and tries is the plural noun with that sense.

clue.text: Chauffeurs possibly rest — van's broken

indicators.note: broken means smashed apart, so the preceding letters are put back together differently

parts.note: the letters of both words used as fodder

explanation.surface: Drivers take a break because their van has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: Chauffeurs are employed drivers, one kind of domestic staff, hence 'possibly' for an example.

clue.text: Incompetent friend found in a former city

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one word goes within the others

parts.note: taken as written
a mate is a friend
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: A useless companion turns up in an ancient ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateur as an adjective means unskilful or inept, as in an amateur job.

clue.text: Shame about missing shoe

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: a scandal is a disgrace or shame
C is circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: It's a pity a shoe has gone astray.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandal is a light open shoe fastened with straps.

clue.text: Concerns a female shows

parts.note: taken as written
F is the abbreviation for female
fairs are exhibitions or shows

explanation.surface: Worries that a woman displays.
explanation.definitionFit: Affairs are matters or business, the things one is concerned with.

clue.text: Darts players who are ranked admitting pressure

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so a letter is placed inside the phrase's word

parts.note: seeds are ranked players in a tournament
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Seeded darts players letting pressure get to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darts' looks like the pub game, but it is a verb meaning dashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move quickly, so darts means rushes, which is what speeds does as a verb.

clue.text: Salesman coming in trim and ready

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: to pare is to trim
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A smart, well-turned-out salesman arriving all set to go.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trim and ready' reads as two adjectives; ready is really the verb, to ready something.
explanation.definitionFit: To ready something is to make it fit for use, the verb meaning to get set up.

clue.text: What you might get from pharmacy, initially, ahead of ailments

definitions.text: What you might get from pharmacy

indicators.note: ahead of puts the single letter in front of the word that follows
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the first letter of pharmacy
ills are ailments

explanation.surface: Getting tablets from the chemist before illnesses take hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pharmacy' does double duty: in the definition and as the source of the opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pills are tablets of medicine, typical items dispensed by a chemist.

clue.text: Bird by middle of night is breathing heavily

parts.note: the puffin is a seabird

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its central letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the central letter of night

explanation.surface: A bird out at night is panting.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffing means blowing out short breaths, as when breathing hard after exertion.

clue.text: Perfect view with lake below

indicators.note: in a down entry, below means placed underneath, so the abbreviation comes last

parts.note: a view is an opinion or idea
L is the abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A flawless vista with a lake beneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Below' is a down-clue placement: L comes beneath, i.e. after, IDEA. 'View' suggests scenery but means opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal as an adjective means flawless or exactly as wished, so perfect.

clue.text: Boy almost allowed large spoon

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lad is a boy
let means allowed

explanation.surface: A boy was nearly permitted a big spoon.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladle is a long-handled deep spoon used for serving soup.

clue.text: Trump perhaps in attendance, restricting international diplomacy at first

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so the first phrase surrounds the letters after it

parts.note: present means in attendance

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letters of the two words before it

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Trump attending, and curbing global diplomacy from the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Donald Trump is a US president, so he is an example, as 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Papa gets out of bed after certain, short rude awakenings

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word before it loses its end

parts.note: sure means certain
Papa is the NATO alphabet word for P
rises means gets up

explanation.surface: Dad hauls himself out of bed after some rude awakenings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts P and RISES after the shortened word.
explanation.definitionFit: Surprises are shocks or unexpected events, and a rude awakening is an idiom for one.

clue.text: Sensible son with old hat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
O is the abbreviation for old
lid is slang for a hat

explanation.surface: A level-headed boy in a vintage hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid can mean dependable and sound in judgment, close to sensible.
